name: Profhilo Body

lead: Profhilo Body is an IBSA hybrid hyaluronic acid injectable used by clinicians to treat laxity and roughness of body skin, such as the upper inner arms and backs of the hands. People use it for smoother, firmer-looking skin there.

It uses hybrid complexes of high- and low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid injected into the skin to improve skin quality rather than add bulk. Published evidence includes a 12-month single-arm study of women with upper-arm laxity, a completed trial on the backs of the hands and a post-marketing safety review. These are small and mostly uncontrolled.

paras: A clinician injects it into the skin of the area in a short course of sessions. Results are described as building over the following weeks.
A post-marketing review has assessed adverse event reports across the product family. Injections carry general risks such as bruising and swelling, and it is given by trained clinicians.

angle.text: People use Profhilo Body to firm and smooth lax or rough skin on the upper arms and backs of the hands. Hybrid hyaluronic acid injected into the skin hydrates and tightens it. Small single-arm trials have studied it.

lead: Profhilo Body is an injectable hybrid hyaluronic acid (HA) product from IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for improving skin quality on the body, including the upper inner arms, abdomen, knees and backs of the hands. It uses the NAHYCO hybrid technology, which forms stable cooperative complexes from high- and low-molecular-weight HA [1][2]. People have it done to firm and smooth loose, crepey or rough-looking skin where they feel the skin has lost tautness, rather than to add volume.

Treatment is given as a series of small injections spread over months, and published studies report outcomes using skin measurements, photographic scales and patient questionnaires. A 2026 systematic review of nine studies with 278 participants on Profhilo and Profhilo Body reported statistically significant changes or trends toward improvement in elasticity, hydration, density and laxity across several body sites, and photographs showing improved turgor, tone and texture [1]. A 12-month single-arm study in women aged 37 to 65 with upper-arm laxity reported a significant drop in laxity scores by month 3, maintained to month 12 [3].

Published evidence is mostly small and uncontrolled, and the product's safety record comes from post-marketing surveillance: for 2020 to 2023, 11 adverse events were recorded for the body product among about 27,692 patients projected as exposed, mostly oedema, redness and discomfort [2].
infobox: Upper inner arms, abdomen, knees, hands [1][3]

paras: Profhilo Body is the body-oriented formulation in the Profhilo range, described in the literature as a skin booster intended to improve skin quality rather than to add volume [2]. The related face product was analysed in post-marketing data from 2018, and the body product from 2020 [2]. Hyaluronic acid more broadly forms a gel with water and is used as a dermal filler lasting about 6 to 12 months [4].

The systematic review of nine studies (278 participants) reported statistically significant changes or trends toward improvement in viscoelasticity, hydration, density and laxity of the neck, inner arms, abdomen, knees and hands, plus improved Wrinkle Severity and Facial Volume Loss scores on the face [1].

In the 12-month upper-arm study, the treatment was two injections one month apart followed by five injections two months apart; 34 participants received the first three injections and 32 the next four, and at least half reported moderate improvement on their own assessment [3].

Post-marketing data for 2018 to 2023 (face) and 2020 to 2023 (body) recorded 371 adverse events for the face product among about 1,091,956 projected patients and 11 for the body product among about 27,692, corresponding to 0.034 percent and 0.040 percent of exposed patients; the most common events were oedema, erythema and discomfort [2]. In the upper-arm study, slight bruising occurred in 36 participants [3]. Wikipedia notes that HA injection in general can cause bruising, redness, itching and, rarely, vascular occlusion or granulomatous reactions [4]. The surveillance data are spontaneous reports rather than controlled comparisons [2].

A systematic review of nine studies covered Profhilo and Profhilo Body [1]. A single-centre, single-arm 12-month study treated women with upper-arm laxity [3]. A registered trial, NCT05590364, assessed an injectable treatment for roughness and laxity of the backs of the hands in 51 participants and is listed as completed [5]. Published evidence consists mainly of uncontrolled studies; no randomised controlled trial of Profhilo Body against a control was found.
